messages:
sam: Heads-up: replicated a customer report — intermittent network caused an SSE stream to cut out. Client reconnected by re-POSTing the same chat stream; server started a fresh generation and the customer got billed twice. Repro steps and traces below.

maria: Ugh. Can you paste the exact curl and the capture? Which endpoint/accept header?

sam: Chat streaming. I used this curl to repro: 
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "X-Client-Id: acme-123" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-4x","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize payroll changes"}]}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams
```
Then I cut network at ~1.2s (tcpkill). After reconnecting by repeating the same POST, the server produced an entire new generation and the ledger shows two charges.

kevin: If the client doesn't present the resume token on reconnect, the server can't resume and will spawn a new gen. Did the original stream include a resume token frame?

sam: Yes, captured SSE frames (trimmed):
```
event: chunk
id: 23
data: {"seq":1,"delta":"Payroll changes: we increased X..."}

event: chunk
id: 24
data: {"seq":2,"delta":"...and adjusted Y due to..."}
event: resume-token
id: 25
data: {"resume_token":"rt_abc123","last_seq":2}
```
Client had last_seq=2. On reconnect I did not send any resume header; server restarted seq from 1 and emitted a new resume token `rt_def456`. Billing lines show two gens.

jordan: Paste the request/response headers from both attempts. Need to confirm whether reconnect attempt sent any resume token header or Idempotency-Key.

sam: First request headers (client->server):
```
POST /v1/streams
Accept: text/event-stream
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
X-Client-Id: acme-123
```
Response was 200 chunked with the events above. Reconnect request was the same; no X-Resume-Token.

kevin: Confirmed expected behavior: resume only works if client sends the resume token via an `X-Resume-Token` header or `?resume_token=` param. Otherwise it's a new generation and billed.

maria: Customer says their library can't be updated for a few days. They want a refund for the duplicate charge and a short-term server-side fix so naive reconnects don't double-bill.

jordan: Billing ledger for acme-123 around that time: 
``
2025-11-11T14:02:17Z, acme-123, gen_id=gen_7a, tokens=512, charge_usd=0.024
2025-11-11T14:02:29Z, acme-123, gen_id=gen_7b, tokens=512, charge_usd=0.024
```
Both charged; gen IDs differ.

kevin: Two mitigation paths:
- Client: update to send `X-Resume-Token` or an `Idempotency-Key` on reconnects.
- Server-side: quick canary dedupe: in-memory short window keyed by `auth_token|prompt_hash|client_id|model` that, if a match exists and the prior run emitted a resume token within that window, returns a control response pointing the client to resume instead of creating a new gen. That avoids duplicate billing for naive reconnects.

maria: Can we flip something immediately for this org while we ship a proper fix? Customer is asking for a refund and to be protected now.

jordan: We can enable a prod canary feature gate `sse_reconnect_dedupe` for selected orgs: 30s LRU cache that stores last_gen_id + resume_token + last_seq. If a new POST matches the cache and resume_token is present, server returns a control SSE event instructing resume and does not bill. Risk: two legitimate identical requests within the window could be collapsed. We'll require match on client id and keep grace window small to reduce collisions.

kevin: Implementation sketch: 
1) Add in-memory LRU dedupe cache (default 30s). Key: `user_id|prompt_hash|model|client_id`. Value: `{last_gen_id, resume_token, last_seq, created_at}`.
2) On incoming POST /v1/streams, before scheduling a generation, check cache. If hit and resume_token available, short-circuit and return a control event to instruct resume (SSE for text/event-stream, 409+JSON for application/json clients). Do not bill.
3) Roll behind `sse_reconnect_dedupe` runtime flag and enable per-org canary.
4) Longer term: persist `Idempotency-Key` support for 24h.

maria: For the immediate customer: issue a refund for the duplicate line and opt them into the canary. Also prepare a support note describing required client headers (X-Resume-Token, Idempotency-Key) and the temporary behavior.

jordan: Creating billing ticket BILL-4821 and issuing a credit for gen_7b. Enabling `sse_reconnect_dedupe` for acme-123 now. Adding an alert to watch for sudden drops in generation rate and for resume_token thrashing. :white_check_mark: 

kevin: I'll open a small PR today with the LRU cache and feature flag. Tests will include: cache hit -> no new gen created; SSE control event emitted; JSON clients get 409 with a resume_required body. Also adding optional `session_hint` JSON payload acceptance for `last_seq` so some middleboxes can help.

sam: That sounds good. We'll update our client to send `X-Resume-Token` on reconnects long term. For now grateful for the canary.

maria: Action items recap: 
- kevin: PR + canary rollout (coord with SRE)
- jordan: refund + BILL-4821 + enable canary for acme-123
- support: contact customer with refund confirmation and steps; update KB
- runtime/infra: plan idempotency-key persistence for longer-term dedupe

system-bot: Incident logged INC-2025-11-11-SSE-REGEN-ACME (support escalated, canary toggle enabled).
